dedupe_keys.name: soilcover one dimensional soil atmosphere water balance model for designing soil covers on acid generating mine waste rock and tailings

description: A model for designing soil covers that keep oxygen and water out of sulphidic tailings and waste rock after mine closure. The paper deposited at the University of British Columbia says SoilCover predicts water exchange between the atmosphere and a soil surface using Darcy's law and Fick's law for liquid water and vapour flow in the soil, with a modified Penman method for evaporation from saturated and unsaturated surfaces, accounting for weather, soil properties and vegetation. It computes a water balance of infiltration, evapotranspiration, runoff, ponding and storage, and changes in water content, suction, vapour pressure, temperature and hydraulic conductivity with depth and time, as a one-dimensional transient analysis whose surface fluxes can drive two-dimensional groundwater models of tailings and waste rock. The DataCite record dates the deposit to 2009; the current distribution, price and licence of the software are not stated on the page read, and the paper is a free download. Coverage is any mine site with climate and soil data. Caveats: a paper describing the model, not the software itself. For simulation it estimates infiltration into waste piles and tailings in wet and dry climates, a driver of seepage and stability. A related catalogue record is the Mount Polley tailings breach review.
